solution.solution: Claude Code's own automatic continue, autoContinueAtUsageLimit, on by default from 2.1.234 in interactive sessions signed in with a claude.ai subscription, carries the work: when a claude.ai usage limit stops Claude mid-task, Claude Code waits in the open session and, at the reset, prompts Claude to pick the task up where it stopped, and starts the wait again each time the task hits the limit, so the run makes nothing, and the user only leaves the session open, with the computer awake, on the night's work.
solution.why: It's Claude Code's documented way for exactly this case (interactive-mode, Wait for a usage limit to reset: "When a claude.ai usage limit stops Claude mid-task, Claude Code waits in the open session and continues the task on its own after the limit resets"; "Claude Code prompts Claude to pick the task up where it stopped"; "If the task hits the limit again, the wait starts again"), needs no install and no instruction from anyone, and goes on in the very open session, whereas overnight, built in this run, rests on StopFailure firing with rate_limit at a claude.ai usage limit, which the hooks reference gives only with "429 Too Many Requests" and nowhere ties to a usage limit, and, where it did fire, its headless resume would run beside Claude Code's own continuing of the same session.

assumption.assumption: Over one night of rn's work, which runs much of itself in subagents, Claude Code's own wait starts at a real claude.ai usage limit and continues the work from where it stopped to its end, within the three automatic continuations after which it stops ("After three automatic continuations, automatic continue stops"), as the docs say nothing of whether work in subagents or other background work falls under the continuing.
assumption.test: On the real thing, in Claude Code 2.1.332 in an interactive session signed in with the user's claude.ai subscription, with autoContinueAtUsageLimit set false in none of the settings files (none sets it now: ~/.claude/settings.json, the repository's .claude/settings.json, and the worktree's hold no such key), overnight not installed, and the computer kept from sleeping, as after a sleep of more than about 30 minutes the wait asks for Enter ("the first line reads `Your usage limit has reset` and the second reads `Press enter to continue`"): leave rn a night's work that runs into the limit, and in the morning read the session for `Usage limit reset · Continuing automatically` and whether the work, its subagents' parts included, went on once from where it stopped and reached its end, or where it stopped and on what, such as a permission prompt or `Automatic continue stopped after repeated usage-limit hits`.
